channel.title: News Officina
channel.description: Independent. These outlets are written with AI from public sources; one editor reads and approves what goes out. Each says how it is made on its own About page.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Europe can train frontier AI. Now pay for the machines to do it again
item.description: JUPITER showed a European team can train a model of nearly a trillion parameters on European hardware. The Gigafactory money is waiting, and the finance ministries have yet to sign.

item.title: Europae Laeva: European supercomputer JUPITER tests near-trillion-parameter training for open AI model
item.description: Domyn says a demonstration run on Europe's first exascale machine could pre-train the open EUROPA model in about four months, though only a fraction of its parameters are active at any moment.

item.title: Europae Dexter: America struck the asteroid. The next strike must be Europe's.
item.description: Hera proves Europe can build the whole science chain, yet the kinetic technique still belongs to one agency and its unknowns are unresolved. ESA's member states should order a European impactor with common money at the next ministerial council.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge with drones as Russia reports record drone interceptions
item.description: Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-backed head of Crimea, said road traffic would be restricted until at least midday. Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 1,336 drones, the highest number since the 2022 invasion began.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Ukrainian drones strike Crimea bridge and close road and rail traffic
item.description: Russia's Defence Ministry reported intercepting 1,336 drones overnight, the highest figure since 2022, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov admitted a weakness in Russian air defence.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Estonia plans to close all three border crossings with Russia from 1 December
item.description: The Interior Minister, Igor Taro, will propose closing the crossings at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula after a thwarted sabotage attempt on defence firm Threod Systems that Estonia blames on Russia's GRU.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Moscow set the fire. Brussels must set the bill.
item.description: Estonia answered the GRU's arson attempt alone, with a border closure from 1 December. On Monday the Foreign Affairs Council can turn one capital's countermeasure into a European act, and it should.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Estonia to propose closing all land border crossings with Russia from December
item.description: The proposal follows a sabotage attempt on the Estonian defence company Threod Systems commissioned by the GRU. Foreign minister Margus Tsahkna plans to discuss more pressure on Russia at Monday's meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels.

item.title: Europae Laeva: ASEAN and China provisionally agree on 80% of South China Sea code, leave binding open
item.description: Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said only one of four major issues is settled and the time the talks need has prevented a final deal in 2026. Singapore takes over the ASEAN chairmanship with the remaining work in 2027.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: GPS jamming suspected as seven aircraft lose position guidance over Schiphol
item.description: The Dutch digital infrastructure inspectorate is investigating, with three sanctioned Russian ships near the suspected source. Eurocontrol has issued new guidelines on the growing problem of satellite navigation interference.

item.title: Nuntii Batavi: Seven aircraft lost GPS near Schiphol amid suspected jamming from the North Sea
item.description: The Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management confirmed on Sunday the disruptions of Monday evening and said aviation safety was not at stake. It is the second such incident in four months, according to NRC, and the inspectorate for digital infrastructure is investigating.

item.title: Leo Batavus: GPS jamming suspected after seven aircraft lose signal at Schiphol
item.description: The aircraft landed safely on back-up systems on Monday evening. Wiseman located the source on the North Sea, where HLN and RFI report six Russian-flagged ships were sailing, and the inspectorate is investigating.

item.title: Europae Laeva: 105 US lawmakers demand answers over Starshield restrictions in Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine says the limits disrupted its drone interception system and began as Trump's envoys prepared to meet Putin. The Commission has called for urgent restoration of full service.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Fund the open ecosystem, not the closed copy
item.description: Imec's Leuven cleanrooms already run High-NA lithography, and Brussels holds the Chips Act 2.0 tools to scale them. Washington is building a copy of Leuven with American interests first.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Maileva breach exposed personal data across 39 million mail references
item.description: The breach hit clients in social housing, health and public services, Cyberattaque.org reported, and by 9 November neither Maileva nor La Poste had published a statement, according to the site Ostraca. The CNIL was notified the same evening the platform was shut down.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Drone hits cargo ship MV Larissa 1, no injuries reported
item.description: Defence Minister Ștefan-Radu Oprea said the impact damaged a crane and an investigation is under way. The Insider reports Romania proposed a joint NATO command for drone protection. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced €50 million for a maritime security hub with Bulgaria.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Drone hits cargo ship near Romania, crane damaged, no one hurt
item.description: The MV Larissa 1 is at least the tenth merchant ship struck near NATO coasts since early October. Romania's defence minister says an investigation is under way.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Drone strikes cargo ship in Romanian waters, defence minister confirms no injuries
item.description: Romania's minister Ștefan-Radu Oprea said an investigation was under way after Friday's strike near Sfântu Gheorghe. The attack is at least the tenth against merchant shipping near NATO coasts since October, according to The Insider.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Garante fines Meta 805 million euros over Facebook gallery access
item.description: The Garante ordered specific consent for the feature, which was on by default for roughly 20 million Android users in Italy. Meta says it will appeal.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Larcher calls France's right and centre candidates to one table, raising pressure on Philippe
item.description: The Senate president wants a method to choose a single 2027 candidate. Philippe, best placed in the polls, has opposed a primary for months. BFMTV says polls show no right or centre candidate would reach the second round. France 24 reports voting intentions point to a possible Le Pen-Mélenchon duel.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Meta's €805 million fine is not enforcement yet
item.description: The Italy ruling counts only if the consent fix is delivered within 60 days, and holds through the appeal Meta will file.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Denmark had the luck. Europe needs the plan.
item.description: Gefion is approaching full capacity and gained a new owner as demand is expected to rise at least sixfold within five years. One Danish supercomputer is luck; a European network of them, owned across borders, would be a plan.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Europe funds the satellite but SpaceX flies it. Stop that.
item.description: A Bremen satellite with paying customers is set to launch on an American rocket, while the €22.1 billion pledged in Bremen sits next to European launch firms that need orders. Buy the rockets and the satellite chain becomes fully European.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: European Commission launches defence campaign as poll finds 71% back an EU army
item.description: The 9 November campaign, called "European defence: protect what matters", promotes joint investment, as a GLOBSEC survey finds wide, though not universal, backing for common defence.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Ukraine strikes Volgograd refinery as analyst says 55% of Russian gasoline output is down
item.description: The Lukoil plant, processing about 15 million tonnes of oil a year, burned after an overnight drone attack, and Rosneft has reinstated fuel sale limits nationwide. Strikes since late October have hit refineries with about 30% of Russia's primary refining capacity.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Europe gets a seat at the next Ukraine talks, but not the deal
item.description: Trump's envoy Kushner announced the move on Thursday, and the Kremlin at once played it down. EU foreign policy chief Kallas said the US cannot negotiate lifting sanctions on Europe's behalf.

item.title: Leo Batavus: Nordic defence ministers agree to develop a joint defence agreement
item.description: The decision of 12 November 2026 would give the Nordic defence cooperation a legal framework. Separately, the Riksdag voted to raise the military service age limit to 47, effective 1 January 2027.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for cyber attack on 700 retail sites
item.description: Paris will propose further sanctions against Iranian entities to its European partners. A Commission spokesperson said it is not the Commission's role to attribute cyber incidents. Iran rejects the accusations, and Paris prosecutors are seeking international arrest warrants.

item.title: Leo Batavus: EU auditors say uneven enforcement blunts Russia sanctions
item.description: Direct trade with Russia fell from 253 billion euros to 58 billion between 2021 and 2025. The European Court of Auditors calls for clearer rules and stronger monitoring, saying the Commission lacks criteria to judge whether the sanctions work.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: EU sanctions cut Russia trade to 58 billion euros but enforcement lags
item.description: Trade fell from 253 billion euros in 2021. The European Court of Auditors says unclear rules and uneven application let firms bypass the bans, and Russia now trades more with India and China.
